_readme: The QA baseline, DEFINED — not the number zero.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The tier-2 gate used to require `qa:count` to be 0. That expectation is not
attainable: 552 of the 687 rows measured on 2026-10-13 are `audit_events`, which migration 0181 has
the SYSTEM write rather than the caller, and which `tests/e2e/cleanupOwnership.ts` deliberately never
deletes except by registered id. A gate that can only be satisfied by destroying the database's own
history is a gate people satisfy destructively — `scripts/clean-test-data.mjs` does table-wide
`DELETE FROM audit_events` to get there.
So the baseline is now defined by OWNERSHIP + EXPECTED FIXTURES, and it fails in BOTH directions:
a row that appeared without being declared is drift, and a row that DISAPPEARED is also drift (that
is the defect this replaces — a lane deleted seven baseline rows and the old gate called it cleaner).
POLICIES, one per table:
history — the system writes these rows as a side effect of using the app, no lane can own them, and
they are reported rather than bounded. `observed` is for review, not enforcement.
exact   — a reviewed inventory: the count must match `expected` in both directions. Every entry
carries `why`, naming which rows they are (fixture, tagged suite fixture, hand-entered).
zero    — nothing legitimate writes these; any row at all is a lane's leftover.
A table that holds rows and is not declared here FAILS. That direction is deliberate: the file can only
become more permissive by being edited and reviewed, never by a new table quietly appearing.
Updating it is a reviewed act. `node scripts/dev/qa-baseline.mjs --propose` prints a draft from the
current database; committing that draft is the review step. No command rewrites this file automatically.
Reviewed 2026-10-13 from `node scripts/dev/qa-attribution.mjs` (687 rows in 15 tables, attributed by
table, shop/tenant, time and the repository's own test tags). Target: the QA project only.

audit_events.why: 0181 — the system writes these, not the caller (measured: customer_payments_update/insert 106 each, customer_payment_recorded 82, sale_created 28, branch_selected 10). cleanupOwnership.ts deletes them only by registered id, and no lane can own the history its own sign-in produces

customers.why: 4 hand-entered (Mehboob in the Baba jaani shop; Ab star / Ab jabait / Ab in Default Shop), 8 tagged suite fixtures (Perm/Inv/Fin/Destruct), 3 QA-prefixed created 2026-10-13. The seeded ids 20000000-…-001..003 are absent — qa:seed e2e restores those

products.why: 5 hand-entered (Lambda, Potash, Test, Besto, K plus) plus 1 in the Baba jaani shop (Lambda arc), 9 tagged suite fixtures (3 named QA Marketplace …, Inv/Fin Test Product, QA Dup-safe Product, QA Product A/B)

product_variants.why: one variant per product for the rows above, plus the two QA_IDS variants 40000000-…-001..002

companies.why: 3 protected fixtures (QA Supplier A = companyA, FK-referenced) + 2 hand-entered (Suncrop in Default Shop, Syngenta in Baba jaani) + the tagged suite fixtures Inv/Fin Test Supplier

sales.why: 12 handed-in SALE-xxxxx from the manual QA sessions (2 of them in the Baba jaani shop) + PERM-SALE-001/002 from the permissions suite

sale_items.why: line items of the 14 sales above (one sale has two lines)

voids.why: voided sales from the 2026-10-11/12 manual QA sessions

customer_payments.why: one hand-entered payment in each of the two shops

supplier_payments.why: one hand-entered payment against QA Supplier A on 2026-10-04

inventory_movements.why: movements written by the manual sales and opening-stock entries above

credit_limit_requests.why: created by the credit-request flow during the 2026-10-11/12 QA sessions

customer_crops.why: hand-entered crop records on the customers above

notifications.why: generated by the manual sales/payments above. Not classified as history: they are per-event rows a lane can own, so a rise here means a lane left its own behind

shop_requests.why: one registration request from 2026-10-06, created through the app's own onboarding flow

activity_log.why: nothing in the app writes here outside the flows the lanes drive, which clean up after themselves

returns.why: return flows exist in lanes that own their rows

payments.why: legacy payment table — no flow writes it

cash_reconciliations.why: no lane leaves a reconciliation behind

reminder_logs.why: reminders are exercised by their own workstream

price_history.why: written only by price changes the lanes clean up

users.why: owner — the account every lane signs in with
sales employee — the employee lanes sign in with
QA Admin — used by the integration suites
QA Employee — used by the permission suites

companies.why: QA Supplier A (companyA) — FK-referenced by supplier_payments and products

isolatedTenant.why: The dedicated tenant the two write lanes need (`setupCompletion`, `dependencyContinuity`): app-created through the real registration flow on 2026-10-04, with a default branch, its four system roles and ZERO business rows. The gate asserts it is still empty, because that emptiness is the lanes' premise and a hand run could fill it
